subtopics.title: Two Models — Relative Frequency and Theoretical Probability

questions.question: The theoretical probability model may only be used when:
options: The experiment has been repeated many times
All outcomes of the experiment are equally likely
The event has more than one outcome
The probability is greater than a half

questions.question: For a fair die, P(greater than four) equals:
A courier logs 250 deliveries, of which 35 were late. The relative frequency of lateness is:
The relative frequency of an event, as the number of trials grows, tends to:
options: Jump around more and more
Drift towards a half
Become exactly zero
Settle down towards the true probability

subtopics.title: Venn Diagrams and the Addition Rule

questions.question: The golden rule for filling in a Venn diagram is:
options: Start with the outside region
Start with the largest circle
Start with the overlap, then subtract outwards
Start with the sample-space total

questions.question: With 75 cricket watchers, 60 rugby watchers and 25 watching both among 150 learners, the number watching NEITHER is:
Naively adding the circles gives 75 + 60 = 135, which is wrong because:
options: The circles are drawn different sizes
The 25 in the overlap were counted twice — once in each circle
The outside region was left out
Probabilities may never be added

questions.question: The addition rule states that P(A or B) equals:
options: P(A) + P(B)
P(A) × P(B)
P(A) + P(B) + P(A and B)
P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B)

questions.question: Events are mutually exclusive when:
options: They cannot happen together — P(A and B) = 0
They always happen together
Their probabilities are equal
They cover the whole sample space

questions.question: On one die roll, P(six or less than three) equals:
Complementary events must satisfy:
options: No overlap only
Equal probabilities
No overlap AND together they exhaust the sample space
Both probabilities greater than a half

questions.question: 'Six' and 'less than three' are mutually exclusive but NOT complementary because:
options: Their probabilities are unequal
They overlap at the outcome six
A die has too many faces for complements
The outcomes 3, 4 and 5 belong to neither event, so the pair does not fill the sample space

subtopics.title: Independent Events and the Product Rule

questions.question: The product rule test says A and B are independent exactly when:
options: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B)
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B)
P(A) = P(B)
P(A and B) = 0

questions.question: For the grade's data — P(cricket) = 0,5, P(rugby) = 0,4, P(both) = 25/150 ≈ 0,167 — the verdict is:
options: Independent, because 0,167 is close to 0,2
Independent, because both sports are popular
Dependent, because 0,167 does not equal the product 0,2
Impossible to test from a Venn diagram

questions.question: Drawing two cards WITHOUT replacement gives dependent events because:
options: Cards are not symmetric objects
The first draw changes the pack the second draw faces
The product rule only works for coins
The two draws happen too quickly

questions.question: Two mutually exclusive events with nonzero probabilities can never be independent because:
options: Their circles are drawn too far apart
Their probabilities always total 1
The addition rule forbids multiplication
If one happens, the other's probability crashes to zero — maximum influence, not none

subtopics.title: Guessing from Symmetry or Counting the Tally

questions.question: Claiming fifty-fifty for a falling drawing pin misuses the theoretical model because:
options: A drawing pin has no symmetry, so its two outcomes are not equally likely
Two outcomes are too few for the model
The pin lands too quickly to observe
Probability cannot be applied to stationery

questions.question: From the tally of 200 throws with 122 point-up, the estimated probability of point-up is:
The tally's behaviour as trials increase is:
options: Always exactly the true probability
Steadily drifting towards fifty-fifty
Jumpy at first, settling near the truth in the long run
Increasingly random

questions.question: The kind of object that legitimately invites the theoretical model is:
options: A slice of buttered toast
A courier's delivery record
A drawing pin
A fair spinner with equal sectors

subtopics.title: Two WhatsApp Groups and the Double-Counted Friends

questions.question: Adding the cricket group's 75 members to the rugby group's 60 overcounts because:
options: The 25 people in both groups appear on both lists and get counted twice
Some members never open the groups
Group lists are always out of date
75 and 60 are not comparable numbers

questions.question: The honest headcount of distinct people in at least one group is:
The minus term in the addition rule exists purely to:
options: Make the answer smaller than 1
Cancel the double-count in the overlap
Remove the people outside both circles
Balance the equation's units

questions.question: The minus may only be skipped when:
options: The two groups have equal membership
The sample space is small
The question says 'at least one'
The events are mutually exclusive — the groups share nobody

questions.question: After four heads in a row, the probability the next flip is heads is:
options: Less than a half — tails is due
More than a half — heads is hot
Exactly a half — the coin has no memory
Exactly a quarter

questions.question: The feeling that 'tails is owed' after a run of heads is called:
options: The gambler's fallacy
The addition rule
The law of large numbers
Complementary bias

questions.question: For independent events, P(heads then heads) is computed as:
The product-rule lie detector calls events DEPENDENT when:
options: The two separate probabilities are unequal
The events cannot happen together
The data set is too small
The actual and-probability does not match the product of the separate probabilities
